'''Lars Ivar Samuelson''' (born 20 December 1948) is a Swedish physicist and professor in [[nanotechnology]] and [[semiconductor electronics]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://scholar.google.com/scholar?hl=en&q=Lars+Samuelson&btnG=&as_sdt=1%2C44&as_sdtp= |title=Lars Samuelson |accessdate=June 25, 2017}}</ref> at [[Lund University]].

== Biography ==
In 1977 Lars Samuelson received his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in physics at [[Lund University]]. Afterwards he went for [[Postdoctoral researcher|post-doc]] at the [[IBM Research|IBM Research Center]] in [[San Jose, California]] between 1978 and 1979, researching display technology and band structure calculations.

In 1981 he became an associate professor (Docent) of physics at [[Lund University]], after which he in 1986 became a professor of semiconductor physics at [[Chalmers University of Technology]]/University of Gothenburg.

In 1988 he became a professor of semiconductor electronics at the Department of Physics at [[Lund University]], and in the same year initiated the creation of Scandinavia's first Nanoscience research center, [[NanoLund|Nanometer structure consortium (nmC)]], later re-named NanoLund.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.svd.se/han-skapar-lekplatser-for-elektroner|title=Han skapar lekplatser för elektroner|last=Wickberg|first=Jenny|work=SvD.se|access-date=2017-05-27|language=sv}}</ref> In 2000 he began to focus the Nanometer structure consortium's research on [[Nanowire]]s.

In 2004, he and his team became one of the first in the world to show how it is possible to combine substances with different structural, electrical and optical properties in a nanowire, allowing basic physics and novel devices to be realized.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sverigesradio.se/sida/avsnitt/647692?programid=412|title=Nanotrådar leder mot energisnål teknik - Vetandets värld|last=Radio|first=Sveriges|website=sverigesradio.se|language=sv|access-date=2017-05-27}}</ref>

Since 2021, he is employed as a professor at [[Southern University of Science and Technology]]<ref>{{cite web | url=https://eee.sustech.edu.cn/?view=lars-samuelson&jsid=18&lang=en | title=Lars Samuelson - Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering }}</ref> in Shenzhen, leading the Institute of Nanoscience and Applications (INA).

Lars Samuelson was awarded the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering Sciences|IVA's]] Great Gold Medal in 2022 for his world-leading research in [[nanotechnology]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.lu.se/artikel/stora-guldmedaljen-till-lars-samuelson-vid-lth |title=Stora guldmedaljen till Lars Samuelson vid LTH |trans-title=The Great Gold Medal to Lars Samuelson at LTH |publisher=Lund University |access-date=2025-07-03 |language=Swedish}}</ref>

He was elected a Foreign Member of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] (CAS) (Class of Mathematics and Physics) in 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nano.lu.se/article/lars-samuelson-new-member-science-academy-china|title=Lars Samuelson new member of Science Academy China|publisher=NanoLund|date=2024-01-11|access-date=2025-07-03}}</ref>

Lars Samuelson became a member of the Royal Physiographic Society in 1998,<ref>{{cite web|title=KUNGL. FYSIOGRAFISKA SÄLLSKAPET I LUND - Ledamotsförteckning|url=https://www.fysiografen.se/sv/om-oss/ledamotsforteckning/|work=fysiografen.se|access-date=2022-09-22|language=sv}}</ref> the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]] (Physics) in 2006<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://kva.se/sv/nyheter/nya-ledamoter-i-fysikklassen|title=Kungl. Vetenskapsakademien|website=kva.se|access-date=2017-05-27}}</ref> and The Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering Sciences in 2007. He became [[Fellow of the Institute of Physics]] in 2004, appointed Einstein Professor of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web | url=https://english.cas.cn/newsroom/archive/china_archive/cn2008/200909/t20090923_42764.shtml | title=CAS Einstein Professorship laureate to give a public talk on nanoscience----Chinese Academy of Sciences }}</ref> in 2008, [[List of American Physical Society Fellows (1998–2010)|American Physical Society Fellow]] in 2009 and fellow international at [[Japan Society of Applied Physics]] in 2020.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.ftf.lth.se/about/news-and-events/single-news/article/lars-samuelson-receives-award-from-the-japan-socie/ | title=Lars Samuelson receives award from the Japan Society of Applied Physics &#124; Division of Solid State Physics }}</ref>

Samuelson is the author of well over 700 articles with h-index 91<ref>https://www.webofscience.com/wos/author/record/A-2171-2010sv</ref> by Web-of-Science (h-index 112 by Google Scholar<ref>https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=wwa82MwAAAAJ&hl=sv</ref>), listed in the top 1% highly cited researchers by Web-of-Science and has given more than 300 plenary/invited talks at international conferences.

He is ranked third on the journal [[Nano Letters]] list of the most productive researchers in nanosciences in the years 2001–2009.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://pubs.acs.org/page/nalefd/anniversary/10/most-prolific.html|title=Most Prolific Authors|website=pubs.acs.org|language=en|access-date=2017-05-27}}</ref>

He is the Founder of four start-up companies coming out of Lund University, QuNano AB, Sol Voltaics AB, Glo AB<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.sydsvenskan.se/2011-05-21/forsta-nanobolaget-nara-genombrottet|title=Första nanobolaget nära genombrottet|work=Sydsvenskan|access-date=2017-05-27|language=sv-SE}}</ref> and Hexagem AB,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://press.almiinvest.se/posts/pressreleases/almi-invest-investerar-i-hexagem |title=Almi Invest investerar i Hexagem |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220828135734/https://press.almiinvest.se/posts/pressreleases/almi-invest-investerar-i-hexagem |archive-date=28 August 2022 |url-status=dead}}</ref> engaged in commercialization of nanomaterials technologies.
